title: What Validation Proves—and Building Study-Specific Checks
section: 1. Three Distinct Layers of Evidence in medusa
text:
1. Three Distinct Layers of Evidence in medusa
Keeping three levels of validation distinct prevents both over-claiming and unnecessary skepticism:

Exact conditional operator identities (algebraic & numerical checks): Once run \(r\)’s HRF, smoothing parameter \(\lambda_v\), adaptive weights, and noise correlation \(\Sigma_{\text{cor}}\) are fixed, deconvolution (\(D_r\)) and de-mixed epoch readout (\(B_{r,\tau}\)) are deterministic linear maps. Identities such as \(\operatorname{Cov}(B_{r,\tau}\varepsilon_r) = \sigma_{\text{obs}}^2 B_{r,\tau}\Sigma_{\text{cor}}B_{r,\tau}^\top\) (Propagating BOLD Noise into Trial SEs), scale invariance under restore_scale = TRUE, and \(B_g G_g = I\) in full-rank finite bases (Latent Connectivity Beyond Per-Trial Disattenuation) hold to machine precision (\(10^{-13}\text{--}10^{-15}\)). They guarantee that the code computes the exact mathematical quantity promised—conditional on the first-stage operators.
Isolated mechanism stress tests (Part IV deep dives & chapter benchmarks): Each mechanism study varies one realistic threat at a time while holding surrounding structure transparent—such as fast/slow neurovascular dispersion against \(\text{AR}(3)\) noise (Autocorrelation Prewhitening Under Fast-TR Event Designs), censored edge lags and serial trial dependence in medusa_multilag_infer() (Simultaneous Bands Across Lags), or unequal regional smoothing \(K_S \neq K_T\) and small-\(S\) clustering in connectivity (Latent Connectivity Beyond Per-Trial Disattenuation). These isolate why an estimator succeeds or breaks down.
End-to-end pipeline Monte Carlo benchmarks (14-Study Validation Suite): Refits the entire sequence (estimate_crossrun_hrf() \(\to\) deconvolve_crossrun_hrf() \(\to\) decon_epoch_regression() \(\to\) mixed_by() / medusa_multilag_infer() / decon_connectivity_repair()) inside every synthetic cohort, capturing how estimation uncertainty in Step 1 HRF selection and Step 2 GCV/RWLS tuning propagates into final population \(p\)-values and confidence intervals.

text:
2. Synthesis Map: Claims Tested vs. Scope Boundaries



Table 17.1: Synthesis of validation benchmarks across Part IV and the 14-study validation suite, paired with empirical scope conditions.





Evidence source
Primary pipeline claim evaluated
Key scope boundary to check in your study




Autocorrelation Prewhitening & Validation Study 12
Two-pass target-excluding REML \(\text{AR}(p)\) refit + Winsorized GLS noise_sd recovers true ACF and full trial covariance \(\Omega_{r,\tau}\) (4–8% Frobenius error vs. 21–28% under single-pass canonical HRF)
Requires \(R \ge 2\) runs (recommended \(R \ge 3\)) and drift/motion confounds modeled so \(\widehat{\rho}\) is not pinned at 0.90; use pooling = "graph" when parcels cross pial/CSF borders.


Propagating BOLD Noise into Trial SEs & Validation Studies 1–4
Operator-propagated se_demixed, (1 - 1/m)^{-1} run-centering calibration, and precision_weight_cohort improve group slope RMSE and maintain nominal mixed-model Type I error
Treats first-stage se_demixed^2 as fixed plug-in variances; requires centering within-person covariates (x_within) and specifying participant random slopes in mixed_by().


Step 1–3 & Validation Studies 5–9, 13–14
3D physiological HRF library (preset = "medusa", normalize = "positive_lobe"), modulator-aware & fractional-ridge HRF scoring (amplitude_model = "auto"), GLMdenoise-style cross-validated noise_pcs = "auto" & < 1/128 Hz DCT drift pre-projection (nuisance_mode = "preproject"), monotone SNR-stratified lambda_mode = "auto", rwls = "auto" glitch protection, and other_event_model = "auto" (T, O) epoch demixing
Sub-second fixed ISIs without inter-phase jitter remain fundamentally collinear under hemodynamic low-pass filtering (audit via Step 0 and diagnose_crossrun_recovery()).


Simultaneous Bands Across Lags & Validation Study 11
Studentized Wishart draws + conditioned spectral deblurring + available-case lag pooling hold Max-|T|, 1D TFCE, omnibus_p, and "unsmoothed" window contrasts near nominal 5% / 95% targets under serial dependence and missing participant edge lags
p_maxT and p_tfce control FWER across lags of one (parcel, term) curve; apply "holm" or "BY" across omnibus_p when testing multiple parcels.


Latent Connectivity, Step 6, & Validation Study 10
Per-trial M-MOMS + multi-lag partialed directed EIV (multilag_control = TRUE) + Adaptive-POET & dynamic covariance regression (shared_error_method = "poet_covreg", shared_error = "auto", variance_confounds) + crosstrial_se = TRUE (\(N=1\) Satterthwaite SEs & cohort HKSJ \(t\)-intervals) remove predictor attenuation, cross-lag blur, and stationary/dynamic shared noise
Pairwise-only condition-flipped noise lacking both a multi-parcel factor signature and a measured variance_confounds envelope—or severe seed–target smoothing mismatch (\(K_S \neq K_T\))—still requires a shared-error sensitivity curve and matched Step 2–3 demixing.

title: What Validation Proves—and Building Study-Specific Checks
section: 3. Building a Study-Specific Calibration on Your Own Schedule
text:
3. Building a Study-Specific Calibration on Your Own Schedule
Whenever an empirical study uses a novel multi-phase trial timing, heavy motion scrubbing, or small cohort size, the most informative validation you can run is a synthetic twin of your exact task geometry. Because read_fmriprep_subject() (Step 0) already extracts each participant’s real events table, run lengths, TR, and framewise-displacement valid_rows masks, you can simulate synthetic BOLD directly on top of your actual empirical design in ~35 lines of R—without peeking at real neural associations:

Lock the estimand and multiplicity rule upfront: Prespecify the target condition, peri-event lag(s), covariates, window contrasts, and parcel-family adjustment ("holm" or "BY").
Keep real onset times, durations, and censor masks intact: Use your cohort’s actual events timestamps, reaction-time durations, and valid_rows scrubbing vectors so collinearity between adjacent task phases and run-end/motion truncation match your study verbatim.
Include both an active parcel and a structured null parcel: Generate voxelwise HRF dispersion from hrf_library(), realistic \(\text{AR}(1)\) temporal noise (\(\rho \approx 0.45\text{--}0.60\)), and—if testing Step 6 PPI—shared cross-parcel background innovations.
Refit the full medusa pipeline in every replicate: Run estimate_crossrun_hrf(), deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(), and decon_epoch_regression() from scratch inside the loop rather than freezing oracle HRFs or smoothing parameters.
Audit bias, CI coverage, null false positives, and gating rates together: Check mean(is.na(decon_demixed)), diagnose_crossrun_recovery()$summary$mean_gain, isSingular() rates in mixed_by(), and empirical 95% coverage.


library(medusa)

# Template: Synthetic twin check on one participant's real empirical schedule & scrub mask
# Assumes `sub01` was loaded via read_fmriprep_subject() in Step 0
tr   <- sub01$tr
cand <- hrf_library(tr = tr, preset = "medusa")
evs  <- split(sub01$events, sub01$events$run)
vrows <- lapply(sub01$confounds$runs, `[[`, "valid_rows")

sim_one_subject <- function(beta_true = 0.40, noise_sd = 0.35, rho = 0.50) {
  parcels <- setNames(rep(c("Active_ROI", "Null_ROI"), each = 6L), paste0("v", 1:12))
  h_act   <- cand[, sample(ncol(cand), 1L)]   # random physiological HRF draw
  h_null  <- cand[, sample(ncol(cand), 1L)]
  bold_sim <- cov_sim <- list()

  for (r in names(evs)) {
    n_t <- nrow(sub01$bold[[r]])
    ev  <- evs[[r]]
    t_idx <- which(ev$condition == "feedback")
    x_mod <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(length(t_idx))))

    # Forward neural impulse series on the real empirical timestamps
    s_act <- s_null <- numeric(n_t)
    grid_t <- (0:(n_t - 1L)) * tr
    for (j in seq_along(t_idx)) {
      imp <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(grid_t / tr - ev$onset[t_idx[j]] / tr))
      s_act  <- s_act  + imp * (1.0 + beta_true * x_mod[j])
      s_null <- s_null + imp * 1.0            # evoked response, zero modulator slope
    }
    y_act  <- as.numeric(stats::convolve(s_act,  rev(h_act),  type = "open"))[seq_len(n_t)]
    y_null <- as.numeric(stats::convolve(s_null, rev(h_null), type = "open"))[seq_len(n_t)]

    ar_draw <- function() as.numeric(stats::arima.sim(list(ar = rho), n = n_t, sd = noise_sd * sqrt(1 - rho^2)))
    Y <- cbind(
      replicate(6L, 100 + y_act  + ar_draw()),
      replicate(6L, 100 + y_null + ar_draw())
    )
    colnames(Y) <- names(parcels)
    bold_sim[[r]] <- Y
    cov_sim[[r]]  <- data.frame(x_within = x_mod)
  }

  hf <- estimate_crossrun_hrf(bold_sim, evs, tr = tr, kernel_grid = cand,
                              amplitude_model = "auto", noise_pcs = "auto",
                              valid_rows = vrows, spatial_groups = parcels, pooling = "parcel")
  dc <- deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(bold_sim, hf, scaling = "noise_sd", penalty = "sobolev",
                                nuisance_mode = "preproject", noise_pcs = "auto")
  decon_epoch_regression(dc, cov_sim, evs, target_condition = "feedback",
                         lags = 0, parcel_groups = parcels, other_event_model = "auto",
                         restore_scale = TRUE, return_panel = TRUE)
}

Looping sim_one_subject() across your cohort’s sub01..subN schedules and feeding the resulting panels into mixed_by() (or decon_connectivity_repair()) gives an exact, pre-data answer to whether your task jitter, run count, and motion censoring support unbiased slope recovery and nominal 5% false-positive control in Null_ROI.

section: 1. Stage-by-Stage Reporting Checklist
text:
1. Stage-by-Stage Reporting Checklist



Table A.1: Essential methodological details to report at each stage of an empirical MEDuSA analysis.





Pipeline stage
Quantities & settings to report in Methods / Supplement
Where to inspect in medusa




Step 0 · Design, BIDS/fMRIPrep & Denoising
Number of runs (\(R\)), trial counts per condition, inter-phase / ITI jitter ranges, TR, output space & atlas parcellation, confound strategy ("24p", "csf_wm" + aroma = "nonaggressive" with aroma_clean_nuisance = TRUE), frame-level $variance_confounds (FD, DVARS, RVT), respiratory FD filter (motion_bandstop_bpm), FD threshold, mean/SD % censored volumes, dummy-scan masking (include_non_steady_state = TRUE), and explicit retention of missed/timeout events
sub$tr, sub$confounds$summary, sub$variance_confounds, table(sub$events$run, sub$events$condition) (Step 0)


Step 1 · Cross-Run HRF, Noise-Pool PCs & \(\text{AR}(p)\) Noise
Candidate HRF manifold (hrf_library(preset = "medusa"), positive-lobe normalization), out-of-sample cross-run fold structure (\(s \neq r\)), training amplitude parameterization (amplitude_model = "auto" / hrf_modulators, fracridge = 0.25), spatial pooling & SNR-adaptive de-shrinking (pooling = "parcel" or "graph", selection_mode = "soft_average"), cross-validated background noise-pool PCs (noise_pcs = "auto", max_noise_pcs = 10L), two-pass REML \(\text{AR}(p)\) order (ar_order = "auto"), and % of units hitting the 0.90 stationarity bound
hrf_fit$training_runs, hrf_fit$selections, hrf_fit$settings$noise_pcs_used, hrf_fit$noise (Step 1)


Step 2 · Continuous Deconvolution
Clock-aligned drift, confound, and noise-pool pre-projection (nuisance_mode = "preproject", highpass = 128, noise_pcs = "auto"), smoothness penalty (penalty = "sobolev"), observation-noise standardization (scaling = "noise_sd"), cross-run SNR-stratified smoothing (lambda_mode = "auto"), task-protected glitch downweighting (rwls = "auto"), observation_mask = "fit", and median conditional self-gain
decon$settings$noise_pcs_used, diagnose_crossrun_recovery(decon, events)$summary (Step 2)


Step 3 · Epoch Readout & Demixing
Target condition, peri-event lag grid (lags), neural source model ("impulse" vs. "duration" + "rate" or "integral"), readout kernel & width, collateral and target demixing (demix_other_events = TRUE, other_event_model = "auto", demix_target_trials = TRUE, demix_ridge = "auto" or 0.05), min_bold_coverage threshold (0.20), and % of trial-lags gated to NA
epochs$panel (is.na(decon_demixed), se_demixed) (Step 3)


Step 4 · Parcel Panels, POET CovReg & Weights
Physical scale restoration (restore_scale = TRUE), biological variance mode (tau2_mode, tau2_shrinkage), Adaptive-POET + covariance regression (shared_error_method = "poet_covreg", variance_confounds, or post-hoc aggregate_decon_panel()), outcome column (decon_demixed), cohort precision weights (precision_weight_cohort), and whether within-run ZCA whitening (whiten_panel = TRUE) was used
epochs$panel (shared_noise_vec), epochs$shared_error_model, epochs$unit_error_cor (Step 4)


Step 5 · Group & Trajectory Models
Within-person vs. between-person predictor decomposition (x_within, x_mean), random-effects structure ((1 + x_within || id) + (1 | id:run)), REML Satterthwaite df (lmerTest) & singularity handling; for trajectories: trajectory_mode, contrast_source = "unsmoothed", n_perm, and study-wide multiplicity family ("holm" or "BY")
group_models$coef_df_reml, traj$coefficients, traj$contrasts, traj$latency (Step 5)


Step 6 · Connectivity & PPI
seed_region, target_region, seed_lag, target_lag, orthogonalize_seed_x, control_target_seed_lag / multilag_control, estimator (method = "mmoms" reported alongside "naive_unweighted"), stationary + dynamic cross-parcel error subtraction (shared_error = "auto"), cross-trial sandwich SEs (crosstrial_se = TRUE, \(N = 1\) Satterthwaite df), HKSJ random-effects \(t\)-intervals, convergence/step-up summary, and unmeasured pairwise shared-error sensitivity
ppi$group, ppi$subjects (r_shared_error, alpha_final, df, converged) (Step 6)







Extracting Cohort QC Descriptives in R
Before drafting your Methods section, summarize censoring, deconvolution gain, and trial retention across your analyzed cohort (\(s = 1, \dots, S\)):

# Assuming `subject_bundles` (Step 0), `subject_decons` (Step 2), and `subject_epochs` (Step 4) are named lists:
censor_pct <- unlist(lapply(subject_bundles, function(x) x$confounds$summary$pct_censored))
self_gain  <- unlist(lapply(names(subject_decons), function(id) {
  diagnose_crossrun_recovery(subject_decons[[id]], events = subject_bundles[[id]]$events)$summary$mean_gain
}))
gated_pct  <- sapply(subject_epochs, function(ep) 100 * mean(is.na(ep$panel$decon_demixed)))

cat(sprintf(
  "Censored volumes: M = %.1f%% (SD = %.1f%%)\nConditional self-gain: Mdn = %.2f (IQR = %.2f)\nGated trial-lags: M = %.1f%% (SD = %.1f%%)\n",
  mean(censor_pct), sd(censor_pct),
  median(self_gain, na.rm = TRUE), IQR(self_gain, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean(gated_pct), sd(gated_pct)
))

title: Appendix A — Reporting MEDuSA in Empirical Papers and Reviewer FAQ
section: 2. Adaptable Manuscript Methods Templates
text:
2. Adaptable Manuscript Methods Templates
Replace bracketed placeholders ([...]) with your study’s acquisition and design parameters, and omit optional clauses that do not apply to your analysis.

Template A: Steps 0–4 — Ingestion, Cross-Run HRF Learning, Deconvolution, and Parcel Readout

Single-trial fMRI deconvolution and parcel panel construction. Preprocessed BOLD time series (fMRIPrep [vXX.X], [MNI152NLin2009cAsym], TR = [0.80] s, [R = 4] runs per participant) were analyzed in R using the medusa package ([v0.1.0]; Hallquist, 2026). Within each run, [non-aggressive ICA-AROMA denoising was applied to BOLD volumes and matched CSF/WM nuisance regressors (Pruim et al., 2015; Lindquist et al., 2019), and] [24-parameter head-motion regressors plus cosine drift bases] were projected on an intact acquisition clock (read_fmriprep_subject()). [To prevent respiration-induced pseudomotion from triggering false framewise-displacement (FD) scrubs at sub-second TR, realignment parameters were notch-filtered across 12–20 breaths/min prior to computing FD (Fair et al., 2020).] Initial non-steady-state volumes and frames exceeding FD > [0.3 / 0.5] mm (M = [X.X]%, SD = [X.X]% of volumes) were masked via clock-preserving observation weights (valid_rows) rather than physically concatenating runs, and missed/timeout trials were retained as a separate nuisance event condition in the forward schedule.
Regional hemodynamic response functions (HRFs) were estimated out of sample across runs (estimate_crossrun_hrf(), amplitude_model = "auto", selection_mode = "soft_average") over a three-dimensional physiological HRF library (hrf_library(preset = "medusa"), positive-lobe normalized) pooled within [Schaefer 200-parcel regions / bilateral cortical-ribbon neighborhoods] with SNR-adaptive canonical de-shrinking, rescuing any zero-mean modulated regions via Empirical-Bayes fractional-ridge trial scoring (fracridge = 0.25). Conditioned on each run’s out-of-sample selected HRF, temporal noise autocorrelation was refit in a second restricted-maximum-likelihood (REML) \(\text{AR}(p)\) pass (ar_order = "auto"), and up to [10] cross-validated background noise-pool temporal principal components (noise_pcs = "auto", Gavish–Donoho + 2-fold spatial bi-cross-validation; Kay et al., 2013) were extracted from task-uninformative cortex (Mdn = [K], IQR = [X] PCs/run). Continuous latent neural activity was reconstructed on the acquisition grid via prewhitened, Sobolev-penalized generalized least squares (deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(), scaling = "noise_sd", nuisance_mode = "preproject", highpass = 128), using monotone SNR-stratified cross-run generalized cross-validation (lambda_mode = "auto") and task-protected outlier downweighting (rwls = "auto").
Event-locked trial estimates around [feedback onset] (lags = [-2 to +6 s]) were extracted via decon_epoch_regression() (source_model = ["impulse" / "duration"], readout_kernel = "triangle", restore_scale = TRUE), subtracting mean and trial-varying collateral spillover from overlapping non-target task phases (demix_other_events = TRUE, other_event_model = "auto") and inverting target-to-target hemodynamic mixing (demix_target_trials = TRUE, demix_ridge = [0.05]) to place trial readouts (decon_demixed) on an additive measurement-error scale (Vig & Hallquist, 2026). Voxels were aggregated into anatomical parcels using cross-run precision weights while propagating temporal and spatial noise innovations into run-centered trial standard errors (se_demixed) and subspace-debiased Adaptive-POET + covariance-regression cross-parcel error models (shared_error_method = "poet_covreg", variance_confounds = sub$variance_confounds; Fan et al., 2013; Hoff & Niu, 2012). Trial-lags with fewer than 20% unmasked causal HRF support (min_bold_coverage = 0.20; [X.X]% of trials) were recorded as missing (NA).




Template B: Step 5 — Population Multilevel and Peri-Event Trajectory Inference

Group-level trial and trajectory inference. Time-varying behavioral predictors ([reward prediction error, RPE]) were decomposed into within-person centered fluctuations ([rpe_within]) and person-level means ([rpe_mean]).
[Option 1 — Planned lag or duration mixed models (mixed_by()):] At each [parcel and planned lag], unshrunken trial readouts (decon_demixed) were fit using linear mixed-effects models (mixed_by() via lmerTest; Kuznetsova et al., 2017) weighted by normalized inverse total trial variance (weights = "precision_weight_cohort"), with random intercepts and within-person slopes per participant and nested run intercepts (decon_demixed ~ rpe_within + rpe_mean + (1 + rpe_within || id) + (1 | id:run)). Degrees of freedom were estimated via Satterthwaite’s approximation, and \(p\)-values across [P = 200 parcels] were controlled using [Holm familywise error / Benjamini–Yekutieli false discovery rate] adjustment.
[Option 2 — Joint multi-lag trajectory inference (medusa_multilag_infer()):] Full peri-event lag profiles ([-2 to +6 s]) were modeled jointly using medusa_multilag_infer() (trajectory_mode = "auto"), combining spectral cross-lag deblurring and uncertainty-propagated penalized splines with [799] finite-sample studentized Wishart draws across available participant lag sets. Within each trajectory, simultaneous 95% confidence bands (Max-|T|), 1D threshold-free cluster-enhanced (1D TFCE) \(p\)-values, and Mahalanobis epoch omnibus tests (omnibus_p) were computed; planned window contrasts ([late 3–5 s minus early 0–2 s]) were evaluated on unsmoothed lag estimates (contrast_source = "unsmoothed"). Across tested parcels, epoch-wide discovery was controlled by applying [Holm / Benjamini–Yekutieli] correction to omnibus_p.




Template C: Step 6 — Trial-Level Functional Connectivity and PPI

Measurement-error-corrected trial connectivity and PPI. Trial-to-trial seed–target coupling and psychophysiological interaction (Target ~ Seed + [Modulator] + Seed:[Modulator]) between [seed parcel] and [target parcel(s)] were estimated using decon_connectivity_repair() (method = "mmoms", shared_error = "auto", crosstrial_se = TRUE, orthogonalize_seed_x = [FALSE / TRUE], use_whitened = FALSE). Within each participant, run-centered predictor measurement-error covariance blocks \(\Psi_i\) constructed from squared trial standard errors (se_demixed^2) were subtracted from sample design cross-products (\(X^\top X\)), while stationary and dynamic confound-modulated cross-parcel error covariances (shared_error_model / shared_noise_vec; Fan et al., 2013; Hoff & Niu, 2012) were subtracted from predictor–outcome cross-products (\(X^\top Y\)) with step-up positive-definiteness regularization (Modified Method of Moments with Step-up Regularization, M-MOMS; Fuller, 1987; Vig & Hallquist, 2026), accompanied by cross-trial sandwich standard errors and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom (crosstrial_se = TRUE). Participant-level M-MOMS slopes were pooled across the cohort (\(S = [N]\)) using leverage-guarded Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman (HKSJ) random-effects \(t\)-intervals, reported alongside uncorrected ordinary least-squares ("naive_unweighted") estimates and sensitivity analyses across hypothesized unmeasured pairwise cross-error correlations.

title: Appendix A — Reporting MEDuSA in Empirical Papers and Reviewer FAQ
section: 3. Peer-Review FAQ: Common Questions and Misconceptions
text:
3. Peer-Review FAQ: Common Questions and Misconceptions

Q1. Does evaluating peri-event lags every 0.5 s or 1.0 s mean MEDuSA achieves sub-TR neural temporal resolution?
No. Evaluating lags on a fine peri-event grid (or across jittered sub-TR event onsets) provides smooth phase alignment relative to stimulus onset, not unlimited neural frequency bandwidth. Because hemodynamic convolution \(H_r\) is a strong low-pass filter and Step 2 applies a positive smoothness penalty \(\lambda_v > 0\) to keep variance finite, recovered neural activity \(\widehat{a}_r(t)\) has a finite temporal point-spread width determined by the resolution operator \(R_r = D_r M_{r,o} H_r\). You can report that effective bandwidth transparently via diagnose_crossrun_recovery(decon) (mean_gain) and rely on medusa_multilag_infer(..., trajectory_mode = "auto") for regularized cross-lag deblurring (Step 2; Step 5).


Q2. Isn’t estimating the HRF from the participant’s own task scans circular (“double dipping”)?
No, for two independent reasons. First, estimate_crossrun_hrf() is strictly out of sample across runs: the HRF kernel applied to deconvolve run \(r\) is selected exclusively from non-target runs \(s \neq r\). Second, HRF selection evaluates overall task-evoked variance explained by event occurrences without access to downstream trial-by-trial behavioral modulators (rpe_within), group contrasts, or connectivity targets. Pass-2 \(\text{AR}(p)\) noise refitting on run \(r\) keeps the cross-fitted HRF completely frozen (Step 1; Autocorrelation Prewhitening).


Q3. How does MEDuSA differ from Mumford et al. (2012) LSS beta-series or a standard parametric GLM?
On slow, well-spaced, single-phase designs where the canonical HRF matches regional vasculature, parametric GLMs, LSS beta-series, and MEDuSA yield closely aligned group inferences. They diverge in three common cognitive neuroscience settings (Conceptual foundations §5): (1) rapid multi-phase trials (cue \(\to\) variable-RT decision \(\to\) feedback), where separate LSS regressions omit modulators on neighboring phases and absorb cue/RT confounds; (2) regions with non-canonical HRF peak delays or dispersion, which MEDuSA learns out of sample per parcel; and (3) biphasic or delayed post-event dynamics that collapse to near zero under a single canonical GLM impulse but emerge clearly across a continuous peri-event lag trajectory.


Q4. Empirical-Bayes shrunken decon_eb has lower trial-wise MSE—why shouldn’t I use it as the outcome in mixed_by()?
Minimum mean-squared error for individual trial predictions is not the same goal as unbiased structural slope estimation across trials (Skrondal & Laake, 2001; Vig & Hallquist, 2026). Because decon_eb shrinks noisy deviations toward the parcel mean by reliability factor \(\kappa_{ri} = \widehat{\tau}^2 / (\widehat{\tau}^2 + s_{ri}^2) < 1\), entering decon_eb on the left-hand side of a regression multiplies the true population slope by \(\bar{\kappa} < 1\)—attenuating group effects by 30–60% when single-trial fMRI reliability is moderate (QC Gallery Pair 3). Entering unshrunk decon_demixed with weights = "precision_weight_cohort" avoids shrinkage bias while still downweighting noisy trials and runs optimally.


Q5. Why set restore_scale = TRUE in Step 3 if Step 2 already standardized each run with scaling = "noise_sd"?
Standardizing each run by its marginal observation-noise SD \(\widehat{\sigma}_{\text{obs}}\) inside Step 2 places the data fidelity term and smoothness penalty \(\lambda_v \|P a_r\|^2\) on a dimensionless SNR scale so GCV smoothing behaves consistently across scanners and runs. If left in noise-SD units for Step 3–5, however, a noisy high-motion run (\(\widehat{\sigma}_{\text{obs}} = 2.0\)) would have its true neural signal divided by twice as much as a clean run (\(\widehat{\sigma}_{\text{obs}} = 1.0\)), shrinking its amplitude relative to clean runs. Setting restore_scale = TRUE multiplies both decon_demixed and se_demixed back by \(\widehat{\sigma}_{\text{obs}}\), placing every run of a parcel onto common physical BOLD units while letting se_demixed and precision_weight_cohort downweight noisy runs cleanly (Step 3; Propagating BOLD Noise into Trial SEs).


Q6. How does Step 6 M-MOMS PPI differ from standard gPPI (McLaren et al., 2012) or LSS beta-series correlations?
Standard BOLD-level PPI multiplies noisy BOLD (or MAP-deconvolved point estimates) by task regressors without accounting for two opposing trial-level error biases: (a) random estimation variance \(s_{S,i}^2\) in the seed readout attenuates both baseline connectivity and PPI interaction slopes toward zero, and (b) stationary or dynamic physiological, vascular, or motion noise shared across brain regions (\(r_{ST,i} > 0\)) inflates apparent coupling and task-modulated PPI. decon_connectivity_repair() forms the interaction on de-mixed trial readouts, subtracts analytical seed error moments \(\Psi_i(s_{S,i}^2)\) from \(X^\top X\), subtracts stationary and dynamic Adaptive-POET + covariance-regression cross-parcel error moments from \(X^\top Y\) (shared_error = "auto"), protects small-sample matrix conditioning (method = "mmoms"), accounts for serial cross-trial overlap via Satterthwaite sandwich SEs (crosstrial_se = TRUE), and pools participant slopes via HKSJ \(t\)-intervals (Step 6; Latent Connectivity Beyond Per-Trial Disattenuation).


Q7. Can I interpret the first lag with p_tfce < .05 as the exact onset time of a neural effect?
No. Just as in cluster-based permutation testing for EEG/MEG and spatial fMRI (Sassenhagen & Draschkow, 2019), 1D threshold-free cluster enhancement (p_tfce) integrates contiguous extent and height across lags to boost sensitivity to sustained deflections; its error guarantee applies to the cluster-enhanced statistic rather than exact onset boundaries. When you want strict familywise localization at individual lags of a trajectory, inspect p_maxT and the simultaneous band [conf.low.sim, conf.high.sim]; when you want continuous timing summaries (peak lag, center-of-mass latency, or full-width at half-maximum), report $latency bootstrap intervals from medusa_multilag_infer() (Simultaneous Bands Across Lags).


Q8. Does Sobolev smoothing across motion-censored frames “hallucinate” trial observations inside scrubbed gaps?
No. Under observation_mask = "fit", censored frames (valid_rows == FALSE) contribute zero data weight during Step 2 while keeping acquisition timestamps exact. In Step 3, decon_epoch_regression() computes the exact fraction of each trial-lag’s forward HRF energy supported by unmasked BOLD frames: if fewer than 20% of causal HRF support was observed (min_bold_coverage = 0.20), that trial-lag is gated directly to NA; if partial scrubbing occurred inside the HRF window, the propagated sandwich variance \(\Omega_{r,\tau}\) automatically inflates se_demixed for that specific trial so downstream precision weights downweight it proportionately (Step 3; QC Gallery Pair 3).


Q9. Does noise_pcs = "auto" induce Global Signal Regression (GSR) anti-correlations or regress out zero-mean task modulators?
No. Unlike whole-brain global signal regression (Murphy et al., 2009), noise_pcs = "auto" constructs its background pool strictly from task-uninformative cortex (status == "fallback_prespecified", excluding active parcels, excluding spatial-graph neighbors, and requiring at least 24 background voxels across \(\ge 8\) parcels). Crucially, Step 1’s amplitude_model = "auto" rescues zero-mean modulated regions (e.g., \(\beta_0 = 0\) signed prediction-error parcels) before forming the background mask so modulated task regions never enter the noise pool, and candidate PCs must pass Gavish–Donoho singular-value thresholding, 2-fold spatial bi-cross-validation, an exact Beta task-design orthogonality test, and spectral/temporal coherence gates—selecting \(K^* = 0\) cleanly whenever pervasive physiological noise is absent (Step 1 §1.5).

Relationship to the medusa R Package
This Quarto book lives in the book/ directory of the standalone medusa R package (0.1.1, excluded from CRAN/tarball builds via .Rbuildignore). Every simulation, figure, and diagnostic table in the active chapters was executed directly against library(medusa)—incorporating the complete modern pipeline architecture:
(Under the hood, computationally intensive 3D/4D NIfTI streaming, cortical-sheet graph filters, batched Cholesky deconvolution solves, and peri-event alignment run in compiled Rcpp/RcppArmadillo kernels while exposing clean R S3 objects.)
For NIfTI matrix and file-backed workflows (read_nifti_ts(), write_nifti_ts(), build_spatial_graph(), align_medusa_ts(), voxelwise_deconvolution(), and evt_align_decon_files()), see the package vignettes (vignettes/medusa-workflows.Rmd and vignettes/medusa-docs.md) and function reference (?read_nifti_ts, ?build_spatial_graph, ?estimate_crossrun_hrf, ?deconvolve_crossrun_hrf, ?align_medusa_ts, ?decon_epoch_regression, ?medusa_multilag_infer, ?decon_connectivity_repair).

text:
Pipeline component
Core medusa functions
Key methodological features




Step 0 · Task design & BIDS/fMRIPrep ingestion
read_fmriprep_subject(), read_bids_events(), read_fmriprep_confounds(), read_fmriprep_aroma(), apply_aroma(), read_nifti_ts()
Multi-run & inter-phase jitter feasibility benchmarks, direct 4D NIfTI ↔︎ T × V matrix extraction with pre-flight geometry checks, BIDS/fMRIPrep/BrainGnomes ingestion with clock-preserving valid_rows, frame-level $variance_confounds extraction (FD, DVARS, RVT), non-aggressive ICA-AROMA partial regression, explicit missed_feedback nuisance event retention, and event_index-keyed trial joins.


Step 1 · Spatial Graph, Cross-Run HRF & AR(\(p\)) noise
build_spatial_graph(), hrf_library(), estimate_crossrun_hrf()
Zero-phase respiratory motion filtering (motion_bandstop_bpm / motion_lowpass_hz), 3D physiological HRF manifold (preset = "medusa"), modulator-aware (hrf_modulators) and Empirical-Bayes fractional-ridge trial HRF scoring (amplitude_model = "auto" / "trial_ridge", low-rank Gram pairwise LR \(F\)-test), SNR/breadth-adaptive canonical de-shrinking, training-only out-of-sample parcel (t_{V-1}-to-\(Z\)) and edge-preserving cortical-sheet pooling (pooling = "graph", local sub-grid cones), GLMdenoise-style cross-validated background noise-pool PCs (noise_pcs = "auto"), and 2-pass target-excluding REML AR(\(p\)) noise refit.


Step 2 · Event-informed continuous deconvolution
deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(), diagnose_crossrun_recovery(), write_nifti_ts(), deconvolve_reglin(), deconvolve_nlreg()
Clock-aligned < 1/128 Hz DCT drift, confound, and cross-validated noise_pcs pre-projection (nuisance_mode = "preproject", highpass = 128) prior to \(|H(\omega)|^{-1}\) amplification & GCV, continuous neural source recovery with monotone SNR-stratified lambda tuning (lambda_mode = "auto", PAVA), whole-brain selected_adjusted_partial_r2-screened task-guarded rwls = "auto" glitch downweighting, outlier-trimmed GLS marginal "noise_sd" scaling, bold-free Step 2 \(\to\) Step 3 bold_obs (\(\le 16{,}384\) voxels) / whitened_sketch (\(> 16{,}384\) voxels) caching, explicit hrf_inverse_operator() strata, and 3D/4D NIfTI export (deconvolve_nlreg() retained as blind Bush & Cisler, 2013 comparator).


Step 3 · Trial-epoch readout, alignment & demixing
decon_epoch_regression(), align_medusa_ts(), evt_align_decon_files()
Local time-averaging (kernel quadrature) onto peri-event lag grids, GCV-stabilized joint (T, O) collateral non-target removal (demix_other_events, other_event_model = "auto"), post-subtraction S_clean_tau duration gain calibration ("rate" vs. "integral"), uniform multi-lag target demixing (demix_target_trials), within-trial lag demixing (demix_within_trial), edge-preserving neighborhood trial-variance shrinkage (tau2_shrinkage = "graph_eb"), exact error propagation (se_demixed), and descriptive peri-event alignment (align_medusa_ts()).


Step 4 · Parcel panels, POET CovReg & cohort weights
decon_epoch_regression(..., parcel_groups = ...), aggregate_decon_panel()
Multi-stratum inverse-variance parcel pooling, subspace-debiased Adaptive-POET + multi-lag Toeplitz & LTZ-gated dynamic covariance regression (shared_error_method = "poet_covreg", variance_confounds, Step-2 rwls frame_weights propagation, \(>512\)-unit lowrank_voxel mode), Block-PAF list-columns (shared_noise_vec, lag_noise_vec, trial_cor_vec) with pipe-delimited CSV/.csv.gz round-trip restoration, post-hoc voxel-to-parcel aggregation (aggregate_decon_panel()), precision_weight & precision_weight_cohort, and paired within-run trial decorrelation (whiten_panel, ZCA).


Step 5 · Group & trajectory inference
mixed_by(), medusa_multilag_infer(), backproject_medusa()
Cohort-weighted split-wise REML mixed models (lmerTest, supporting disk-backed Parquet/.rds/CSV streaming and split_filter pushdown), joint multi-lag trajectories with available-case pooling, conditioned spectral cross-lag deblurring (alpha1 = 0.05, alpha0_sq = 0.020), uncertainty-aware penalized splines (Marra–Wood), finite-sample covariance draws (studentized Wishart) for Max-|T| / 1D TFCE / omnibus tests, "unsmoothed" window contrasts, and NIfTI map backprojection.


Step 6 · Trial connectivity & PPI
decon_connectivity_repair(), medusa_fit_mmom(), medusa_between_subject_repair()
Within-trial predictor disattenuation with conditioning protection (M-MOMS), joint multi-lag partialed directed EIV connectivity (multilag_control = TRUE, control_seed_lags), stationary & dynamic cross-parcel shared_error = "auto" subtraction (including on-the-fly dynamic modulator evaluation when Step 3 ran marginally with covariates = NULL), exact residualized-seed covariance projection, single-subject (\(N=1\)) & subject-level cross-trial sandwich SEs + Satterthwaite df (crosstrial_se = TRUE), and finite-sample random-effects \(t\)-interval pooling (HKSJ).

section: Reproducing All Simulations, Figures, and the Book
text:
Reproducing All Simulations, Figures, and the Book
With medusa and its plotting/reporting dependencies (ggplot2, data.table, lmerTest, knitr, rmarkdown; plus ggbrain, patchwork, and RNifti when regenerating volumetric brain-map figures) installed in R, render the book from book/:
quarto render
Because quarto render reads the saved .rds and .csv outputs generated by each chapter’s standalone scripts, rendering completes in seconds. To regenerate every simulation, diagnostic table, and figure from scratch against the installed medusa package, run the chapter scripts below from book/:


Show full simulation and figure regeneration commands

# Quickstart workflow map & signal walkthrough, forward-model, dataflow schematic, & GLM/FIR/LSS/MEDuSA benchmark
Rscript assets/quickstart-figures.R
Rscript assets/forward-model.R
Rscript assets/pipeline-dataflow.R
Rscript assets/compare_glm_fir_lss_medusa.R

# End-to-end worked example & M-MOM covariance verification
(cd worked && Rscript run.R && Rscript mmom-check.R && Rscript checkpoints.R)

# Step 0: Experimental design benchmarks & BIDS/fMRIPrep subject ingestion
(cd medusa_step0_design_bids && Rscript simulate_step0.R && Rscript figures_step0.R)

# Step 1: Cross-run HRF & AR(p) noise + Woolrich noise review
(cd medusa_step1_hrf_noise && Rscript simulate_step1.R && Rscript figures_step1.R)
(cd medusa_step1_hrf_noise/woolrich_review && Rscript compare_noise.R && Rscript variance_check.R && Rscript plot_comparison.R)

# Step 2: Event-informed continuous deconvolution (including blind vs. event-informed benchmark)
(cd medusa_step2_deconvolution && Rscript simulate_step2.R && Rscript figures_step2.R)

# Step 3: Peri-event epoch readout & demixing
(cd medusa_step3_epochs && Rscript simulate_step3.R && Rscript figures_step3.R)

# Step 4: Parcel aggregation, shared noise loadings, & cohort precision weights
(cd medusa_step4_parcel_panels && Rscript simulate_step4.R && Rscript figures_step4.R)

# Step 5: Split-wise mixed models & joint multi-lag trajectory inference
(cd medusa_step5_group_models && Rscript simulate_step5.R && Rscript figures_step5.R && Rscript simulate_pr62.R && Rscript figures_pr62.R)

# Multi-lag trajectory empirical calibration (180 replications x 2 regimes)
(cd medusa_multilag_calibration && Rscript simulate.R && Rscript figures.R)

# Step 6: Trial-level connectivity, M-MOMS, & PPI sensitivity
(cd medusa_step6_connectivity && Rscript simulate.R && Rscript figures.R)
(cd medusa_connectivity_inference && Rscript prepare_figures.R)

# Volumetric spatial & parcel pooling benchmark + ggbrain maps
(cd medusa_spatial_parcel_pooling && Rscript simulate_spatial_pooling.R && Rscript figures_spatial_pooling.R)

# Visual QC & troubleshooting gallery across Steps 0-6
(cd medusa_qc_gallery && Rscript simulate_qc_gallery.R && Rscript figures_qc_gallery.R)

# Render full Quarto HTML book to _book/
quarto render
